--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The task is from evolutionary tournament, parent slot 5 fitness 258.5. Need produce new strategy likely better."
STRATEGY: Parent is a conditional strategy that cooperates early, defects if opponent never defects after round 20, retaliates against defection, and has endgame logic. The trace simulates the parent and other population strategies against candidate probes, and considers changing the strategy to exploit unconditional cooperators and forgiving opponents while avoiding retaliation.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "So optimal against slot 3 is to defect for 6 rounds, then cooperate. That gives 312. Compare to always cooperate: 300. So we can gain 12 points by defecting first 6 rounds."
STRATEGY: The parent is a rule-based IPD strategy that cooperates by default, retaliates to defections, and defects at the endgame. The trace simulates specific opponents (slot 3, slot 9, slot 6, slot 1) by reading their source code and estimating payoffs. It proposes changes: probing with an early defection, adaptive exploitation of forgiving opponents, and last-round defection.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Given the fitness values, the top strategies don't exploit much; they mostly cooperate." / "So a simple TFT with last-round defect might actually score higher than the parent!"
STRATEGY: The parent is a probe-then-adapt strategy (C, D, C probe, then exploit/TFT). The trace simulates it against always-C, always-D, slot1, slot3, and slot9, and revises it toward a TFT-with-last-round-defect plus limited early defection, using the probe's retaliation to decide whether to keep exploiting.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's look at the parent's weaknesses. The parent has complex endgame logic. It might make mistakes. A simple TFT is often very strong in these tournaments."
STRATEGY: The parent is a complex endgame strategy with TFT-like retaliation and last-round defection. The trace simulates candidate revisions against population slots (slot1, slot3, slot6, always-C) and computes payoffs. It changes the strategy to TFT with last-round defect plus occasional probing when the opponent has never defected.

--- PART 5/5 ---

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So this strategy is simple, robust, and improves on the parent. It should score higher than 258.5."
STRATEGY: Parent is TFT with occasional probes when the opponent has never defected. Simulated against slot1, slot3, slot6, always C, always D, and slot9. Changed to add a final-round defection at n==99, an aggressive-opponent rule, and single probes at n%10==0 when opp_defects==0 and n>50.
